summary: This informational document defines TLS cipher suites that use the ARIA block cipher, a Korean encryption standard. Adding them lets TLS connections use ARIA for encrypting data. It is not on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: When two computers set up a secure connection, they agree on one named set of algorithms for protecting the data, and that set is called a cipher suite. This document adds cipher suites that use ARIA, a block cipher designed in Korea, together with SHA-256 or SHA-384.

questions: what is aria cipher in tls
which tls cipher suites use aria
subtitle: TLS cipher suites that add the ARIA block cipher, with SHA-2 hashes, Galois Counter Mode and pre-shared key variants.

tldr.problem: TLS could not use ARIA, a block cipher that is a Korean standard and is widely used in Korea, because no cipher suite defined it.
tldr.mechanism: The document defines suites that pair ARIA with the key exchanges of TLS 1.2, using ARIA in CBC mode with a SHA-2 HMAC or ARIA in Galois Counter Mode, plus pre-shared key variants.
tldr.outcome: IANA allocated the code points 0xC0,0x3C through 0xC0,0x71 in the TLS Cipher Suite Registry. The document is Informational rather than a standard, and it has since been updated by RFC 10015.

today: RFC 6209 is an Informational document, not an Internet Standards Track specification, and it has been updated by RFC 10015. It was not obsoleted.

sections.title: Why ARIA Needs TLS Cipher Suites
sections.content:
This document specifies cipher suites for the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol so that the ARIA encryption algorithm can be used as a block cipher. It builds on RFC 5246, which defines TLS 1.2, and on RFC 5794, which describes ARIA.

The suites use the SHA-2 family of cryptographic hash functions and ARIA in Galois Counter Mode. Elliptic curve cipher suites and pre-shared key (PSK) cipher suites are also defined. Suites that use SHA-1 are left out on purpose: recent analytic work on SHA-1 led the IETF to move gradually away from SHA-1 and towards stronger hash algorithms.
sections.plainLanguage: Before a secure connection starts, the two sides agree on one cipher suite, which names the cipher and the hash function they will use. This document adds suites that use ARIA, a cipher designed in Korea, and it leaves out SHA-1 because the IETF is moving to stronger hashes.

sections.title: The ARIA Cipher
sections.content:
ARIA is a general-purpose block cipher algorithm developed by Korean cryptographers in 2003. It is an iterated block cipher with 128-, 192- and 256-bit keys, and it encrypts 128-bit blocks in 12, 14 or 16 rounds, depending on the key size. The RFC says it is secure and suitable for most software and hardware implementations on 32-bit and 8-bit processors.

It was established as a Korean standard block cipher algorithm in 2004 and has been widely used in Korea, especially for government-to-public services. It was included in PKCS #11 in 2007. The algorithm specification and its object identifiers are described in RFC 5794, not in this document.
sections.plainLanguage: ARIA is a block cipher from Korea. It encrypts a block of 128 bits at a time, repeating its encryption step 12, 14 or 16 times depending on whether the key is 128, 192 or 256 bits long.

sections.title: The Three Groups of Cipher Suites
sections.content:
The suites come in three groups. The first twenty use ARIA in Cipher Block Chaining (CBC) mode with a SHA-2 family Hashed Message Authentication Code (HMAC); eight of those twenty use elliptic curves. The next twenty use the same asymmetric algorithms as the first group but use the authenticated encryption modes defined for TLS 1.2, with ARIA in Galois Counter Mode (GCM).

The last fourteen are PSK suites: eight use an HMAC and six use ARIA in Galois Counter Mode. Names follow the pattern TLS_RSA_WITH_ARIA_128_CBC_SHA256, where the key exchange comes first, then the cipher and the key size, then the hash. The 128-bit suites end in SHA256 and the 256-bit suites in SHA384.
sections.plainLanguage: The document lists three sets of suites. One set uses ARIA in CBC mode and adds a separate HMAC check on the data; one set uses ARIA in Galois Counter Mode, which encrypts and checks the data in one step; the last set is for devices that already share a secret key.

sections.title: Key Exchange, Cipher and Pseudorandom Function
sections.content:
The RSA, DHE_RSA, DH_RSA, DHE_DSS, DH_DSS, DH_anon, ECDH and ECDHE key exchanges are performed as defined in RFC 5246. The ARIA_128_CBC suites use a 128-bit key and a 128-bit initialization vector (IV); the ARIA_256_CBC suites use a 256-bit key and a 128-bit IV.

The GCM suites are defined by analogy with AES GCM, described in RFC 5116 and RFC 5288, because AES and ARIA share common characteristics, including key sizes and block length. The pseudorandom function (PRF) SHALL be the TLS PRF using SHA-256 for cipher suites ending in _SHA256, and SHA-384 for suites ending in _SHA384. The pre-shared key cipher suites are described in RFC 4279, RFC 4785, RFC 5487 and RFC 5489.
sections.plainLanguage: These suites reuse the key exchange that TLS 1.2 already defines and only change the cipher. The 128-bit CBC suites use a 128-bit key and a 128-bit initialization vector; the 256-bit ones use a 256-bit key and the same 128-bit vector.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
At the time of writing this document, no security problems had been found on ARIA. The RFC points to a paper on integral attacks against the reduced-round version of ARIA as the reference for that statement.

The security considerations in RFC 4279, RFC 4785, RFC 5116, RFC 5288, RFC 5289, RFC 5487 and the NIST GCM specification apply to this document as well. The document adds no security analysis of its own beyond that.
sections.plainLanguage: When this was written, nobody had found a way to break ARIA. The safety rules that already apply to the older, similar suites apply here as well.

sections.title: IANA Considerations
sections.content:
IANA has allocated the numbers for these suites in the TLS Cipher Suite Registry. The values run from { 0xC0,0x3C }, the code point of TLS_RSA_WITH_ARIA_128_CBC_SHA256, to { 0xC0,0x71 }, the code point of TLS_ECDHE_PSK_WITH_ARIA_256_CBC_SHA384, in the same order as the suites are listed in the document.

The section repeats the full list of allocations, so the registry entries and the suite list in the document are the same information in two forms.
sections.plainLanguage: Every suite in the document was given a fixed number in the official registry of TLS cipher suites, running from 0xC0,0x3C to 0xC0,0x71.

items.label: TLS_RSA_WITH_ARIA_128_CBC_SHA256
items.desc: First suite in the document: RSA key exchange, ARIA in CBC mode with a 128-bit key, SHA-256.

items.label: TLS_ECDH_RSA_WITH_ARIA_256_CBC_SHA384
items.desc: Last of the twenty HMAC-based suites; elliptic curve key agreement.

items.label: TLS_RSA_WITH_ARIA_128_GCM_SHA256
items.desc: First of the twenty GCM suites.

items.label: TLS_ECDH_RSA_WITH_ARIA_256_GCM_SHA384
items.desc: Last of the twenty GCM suites.

items.label: TLS_PSK_WITH_ARIA_128_CBC_SHA256
items.desc: First of the fourteen pre-shared key suites.
